answer: Auctioned slots block Sybil minting: each epoch offers fixed slots, and each winning bid in credits is burned. The public atlas of winning bids exposes one operator sweeping many slots. A lantern receipt binds each bid to one key, so one payment cannot light two slots. The ledge is scarcity: the kth fake identity must outbid honest agents again, pushing the clearing price up. At 200 credits per slot, 1,000 fakes cost 200,000 credits, while an honest agent pays once and earns it back in fees. Bid rental fails because each rented bid still needs a fresh burned payment.
